chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 278 – The Shocking Identity of the County’s Ghost
chapter_meta_description: The ghost is dead, Pi County celebrates, but Li Huowang slips away to the mortuary. The corpse he finds there has a very different story to tell.
og_title: The Feast and the Corpse – Chapter 278 Analysis
og_description: Victory in Pi County yields a feast and fireworks, but Li Huowang’s night has just begun. A dead body in the morgue opens its eyes and reveals a greater power at play.
twitter_title: Dead man talks in the morgue – Li Huowang meets the Supervisory Heavenly Office
twitter_description: Everyone’s celebrating the ghost’s death, but Li Huowang is already one step ahead, interrogating a corpse that isn’t quite dead.

lore_anchors.definition: A government-sponsored supernatural enforcement agency operating under the imperial board of war in the Dao-Twisted World. They investigate abnormal phenomena, hunt rogue cultivators, and manage Heavenly Calamities.
A local administrative record of major events; an empty or sanitized gazetteer in the Dao-Twisted World signals official complicity or denial of supernatural horror.
In Chinese funeral tradition, green or white couplets replace red ones on the doors of a house where a death has occurred. They serve as a stark visual marker of mourning amid celebration.

A fictional sect in the novel that fuses elements of Zoroastrianism (袄教) and Nestorian Christianity (景教); the original owners of the *Thousand Greats Record*. Li Huowang borrows the alias of its dead member, Jiang Yingzi.
The Ao-Jing sect name used by the Ao-Jing defector Jiang Yingzi; Li Huowang adopts it as a cover identity when dealing with the Supervisory Heavenly Office.
